payload.diff:
## CANON-054 — Public Stats Surface (ACTIVE, STRONG for public-*)

Every VaultSpark website MUST publish a stats surface on its own domain —
canonically `/stats` — reporting the numbers that matter for what the product
actually is (players, accounts, clients, projects shipped).

### Report AND analyze
A bare counter is telemetry, not analysis. Each metric carries: value, period,
computed-at, what is counted (the denominator), and at least one metric per site
must carry a real interpretation a reader could not derive from the number alone.

### Honesty rules (CANON-031 at full force)
- Never fabricate, extrapolate, or round up. No seeded or demo figures.
- **Zero is publishable.** A project with two users publishes two. Waiting until
  the number looks good, or picking metrics because they are large, is the
  failure this canon exists to prevent.
- **Unmeasured is not zero.** An unreachable source renders unavailable with a
  reason — never as 0, never as a stale value shown as current.
- Every number is dated. Say what is counted.

### Privacy (hard boundary)
Aggregate only. Never publish or make derivable individual identities, contact
details, IP addresses, precise locations, or per-user activity. Band any cell
small enough to identify a person. Client-level numbers require that client's
explicit permission.

### Cost + dual-audience
Precompute to a static artifact (CANON-029) — a live query per visitor is a cost
surface. Ship a machine-readable twin referenced from /agents.json and
/.well-known/llms.txt (CANON-048).

### Checker
`node ../vaultspark-studio-ops/scripts/check-stats-surface.mjs --project . --json`

It verifies STRUCTURE and honesty affordances only. No probe can confirm a
published number is TRUE — a fabricated statistic passes the gate and remains a
CANON-031 violation caught by review.

payload.title: Surface Follow-Through — every project change reaches the thing people touch
payload.diff:
## CANON-055 — Surface Follow-Through (ACTIVE, STRONG where a user surface exists)

A session that changes a project MUST also move that project's user-facing
surface — website, app, game, platform, or tool. Backend, schema, tooling and
refactor work is not finished when the internals are correct; it is finished when
the change is REACHABLE.

### What counts
A new or improved interface element; a visible defect fixed; a copy, clarity,
accessibility or performance improvement a user would notice; surfacing new data
the change made possible; or a visible removal that simplifies. Version bumps,
comments, tests and regenerated artifacts nobody sees do NOT count.

### Honest exemptions — declare, never skip silently
`no-user-surface` · `security-incident` · `invisible-by-contract` ·
`deferred-to-task` (valid only if the follow-up task exists).
An exemption is a recorded decision. "Nothing to show" with no reason is the gap.

### This is NOT a change quota
A gratuitous UI edit made to satisfy a checker is WORSE than an honest exemption:
it churns a surface users depend on to produce a green box — a CANON-031
violation. Surface work inherits CANON-053 rendered-pixel review, CANON-041
mobile parity, and CANON-047 theme readability.

### Checker
`node ../vaultspark-studio-ops/scripts/check-surface-followthrough.mjs --project . --json`

Structural only: it classifies changed files as surface-reaching vs internal and
treats a declared exemption as first-class. A file path cannot prove a user-visible
IMPROVEMENT — that is review-enforced.

payload.defect1:
Gap reasons render as a literal '}'. runScriptChecker() parses only the LAST LINE of the checker's stdout (JSON.parse(out.split('
').pop())). Checkers emit pretty-printed JSON, so the last line is the closing brace, JSON.parse throws, parsed stays null, and the detail fallback prints that same brace. payload.rootCause: secrets/CAPABILITY_MAP.json documented TWO credential planes for cloudflare.deploy (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN narrow: Workers 200/Pages 403; CLOUDFLARE_STUDIO_TOKEN broad: Pages 200) and asserted that scripts/lib/cf-deploy.mjs 'already implements exactly this split, and that design is CORRECT'. Three existing callers (domain check, site deploy, rollback) never passed a plane, so a remember-to-pass-it design would have failed again at the next call site. Keep Workers on the narrow token so the fix does not promote everything onto the broad credential. Note CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is wrangler's env-var INTERFACE — a Pages deploy must place the Pages-scoped token in that variable; conflating the variable NAME with a specific credential is what produced the 403.

(3) Re-probe every founder-blocked label live before repeating it in a handoff: two such labels dissolved under live probes in this one session. Supersession between two measurements of one property must be symmetric. A newer file-level green could retire an older assertion-level red but never the reverse, so a 34h-stale cache outranked a fresh full-suite green forever.

## CANON-020 — Analytica is the canonical Studio analytics + insight plane

**Status:** ACTIVE — S119; **expanded S274** (universal ingest plane — Analytica Feed v1). | **Last confirmed:** 2026-08-09.
**Effective:** 2026-05-19; expansion effective 2026-08-09.
**Origin:** Founder strategic decision (S119) — every project needs analytics, the studio has the richest cross-portfolio telemetry surface in the industry (IGNIS + SIL + Ark + GO_OUTCOMES + 27-repo registry), and no competitor can replicate the ecosystem-level signals (cross-pollination, cascade unblocks, canon-coherence drift). Built as the **Insight Layer** on top of the S134 Oracle backbone, not a separate product. **Expanded by Studio Owner directive (S274)** — Analytica must be able to *draw live statistics back from every project*, internal, external, or hybrid, into one founder dashboard.

**Rule.** All studio-wide analytics, cross-portfolio insights, and per-project metric narration flow through Analytica. The three-layer architecture is canonical:

0. **Layer 0 — Ingest: Analytica Feed v1** (S274). Every project — internal, external, or hybrid — **emits one document in one schema** describing its own live statistics. This is the universal ingest contract; Analytica reads nothing bespoke. Spec: `docs/ANALYTICA_FEED_SPEC.md`; schema: `docs/schemas/analytica-feed-v1.json`; collector: `scripts/collect-analytica-feeds.mjs` → `portfolio/ANALYTICA_FEEDS.json`.
1. **Layer 1 — Collectors** (already shipped): IGNIS · Ark · SIL · GO_OUTCOMES · web vitals · social feeds · GitHub events · Stripe events
2. **Layer 2 — Aggregation + Scoring**: `scripts/build-analytica-dashboard.mjs` → `portfolio/ANALYTICA_DASHBOARD.json`. Four proprietary scores: Portfolio Leverage · Cross-Pollination Index · Canon Coherence Drift · Founder Bottleneck Detector.
3. **Layer 3 — Analytica Voice** (Oracle persona): `scripts/lib/analytica-voice.mjs` narrates metrics per project tuned to `context/SOUL.md`. Hybrid model — one Studio-wide Analytica Oracle + per-project SOUL.md persona overlays + IGNIS as the empirical spine.

**Visibility.** Internal-core + opt-in per-project public `/insights` page + embeddable share badge. The aggregation IP stays proprietary; per-project insight summaries are the public signal. A selectively-open metrics-format spec (`docs/schemas/analytica-dashboard-v1.json`) enables long-term ecosystem adoption without giving away the moat.

### The ingest plane — one schema, three transports (S274)

**Every project publishes an Analytica Feed.** The feed is a single JSON document listing that project's live metrics with their values, periods, as-of times, denominators, and interpretations. **It is the same artifact the project's own public stats surface renders from (CANON-054)** — the founder dashboard and the public page read one source, so they can never disagree. A project must not maintain a separate founder-only reporting path; divergence between what the public sees and what the founder sees is precisely the failure this design forecloses.

How the feed reaches Analytica depends only on what the project *is* — the schema never changes:

| Project | Transport | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| **External / public** | `http` — public endpoint | Analytica polls the feed URL declared in the registry. No authentication, no SDK, no per-project integration code: if the URL serves valid Feed v1, ingest works. |
| **Internal / private** | `ark` — cargo, or `local` — file read | Emit `stats-feed` cargo to studio-ops (CANON-018), or write the feed to a local artifact the collector reads from the sibling checkout. Nothing is exposed publicly. |
| **Hybrid** | `http` public subset + `ark` private detail | Publish the visitor-appropriate metrics; ship the sensitive ones privately. Both are Feed v1; the collector merges them by project and metric id. |

**Design constraints, and the reasoning behind them.** Ingest is *pull-and-emit*, never a runtime dependency: no project ever calls into Analytica to serve a request, so Analytica being down, slow, or mid-deploy can never degrade a live product. There is **no client library to install** — a static JSON file at a known location satisfies the contract in any stack, which is what makes "implementable on every project" true rather than aspirational. Metrics are **aggregate only**; CANON-028 and CANON-054's privacy boundary apply to the private transports exactly as they do to the public one, because a founder dashboard is not an exemption from data-protection discipline.

**Honesty on ingest (CANON-031).** The collector records, per project, whether the feed was **reached**, and stamps what it got. A feed it could not fetch is `unreachable` — never `0`, never last-known-value silently re-presented as current. A metric whose declared freshness has lapsed is carried through to the dashboard **marked stale**, not quietly refreshed. The dashboard's own coverage figure ("N of M projects reporting") counts only projects whose feed was actually read this cycle. **An aggregate assembled from unreachable sources is a non-measurement, and reports itself as one.**

**Founder access surfaces.** The collected corpus is queryable three ways, all reading the same `portfolio/ANALYTICA_FEEDS.json`: the **script** (`collect-analytica-feeds.mjs --summary`), the **studio-ops MCP tool** (`studio_analytica_feeds`) for agent and conversational access, and the **Analytica dashboard** itself. Adding a surface never means adding an ingest path.

**Enforcement.**
- `scripts/build-analytica-dashboard.mjs` runs nightly via cron + closeout autopilot Step 3n.
- `scripts/collect-analytica-feeds.mjs` refreshes `portfolio/ANALYTICA_FEEDS.json` on the same cadence; doctor probe `analytica-feed-coverage` reports how many applicable projects are actually reporting and names the ones that are not.
- Doctor probe `analytica-freshness` warns if `ANALYTICA_DASHBOARD.json` >48h stale.
- Brief tile ANALYTICA SNAPSHOT surfaces top-1 insight + top bottleneck on every /start.
- New initiate scaffolding includes `context/ANALYTICS_HOOKS.md` — collectors specific to project medium — and the Feed v1 descriptor template.

**Decision:** D-S119.1 — Analytica elevated to canonical analytics + insight plane for the studio. Spec at `docs/ANALYTICA_SPEC.md`.

payload.diff:
## CANON-054 — Public Stats Surface: every website reports and analyzes its own numbers

**Status:** ACTIVE — S271; **expanded S274** (live homepage tile · project-tailored metric selection · liveness contract · Analytica Feed binding). | **Tier:** STRONG for `audience: public-*`; ADVISORY for internal/private surfaces; not applicable to unlaunched repos with no deployed surface. | **Last confirmed:** 2026-08-09. | **Effective:** 2026-08-06; expansion effective 2026-08-09. | **Source:** Studio Owner directive (S271 — every website should report and analyze its user/app/project/game/client statistics on its own site); expanded by Studio Owner directive (S274 — every external-facing project showcases live, continuously-updating user/community stats on the homepage *and* an in-depth stats page, customized to what that product's visitors actually value, and Analytica draws them all back to the founder dashboard).

**Decision.** Every VaultSpark website **MUST publish a stats surface on its own domain** that reports and *analyzes* the numbers that matter for what that product actually is. A game reports player and match numbers; a software-as-a-service (SaaS) product reports account and usage numbers; a client-services project reports engagement and delivery numbers; a portfolio or studio site reports project and shipping numbers. The surface is a real page — canonically `/stats` — reachable from site navigation, not a hidden route, not a dashboard behind an admin login, and not a third-party analytics console the public cannot see.

### Two surfaces, not one (S274)

Publishing the numbers only where a curious visitor goes looking is not showcasing them. Every external-facing project ships **both** surfaces, and they are different jobs:

1. **The homepage showcase tile — `MUST`, live.** A visible block on the site's landing page carrying a **small curated set** (canonically **three to six** figures) of that product's most compelling live numbers. It is a *showcase*: the numbers a first-time visitor should see without asking, chosen because they convey scale, momentum, or life in the product. It updates continuously per the liveness contract below — a hard-coded number in the markup is a violation of this canon **and** of CANON-031. It links to `/stats`.
2. **The in-depth stats page — `MUST`, deep.** `/stats` goes materially further than the tile: the full metric set, breakdowns and segments, history and trend over time, definitions of what each figure counts, and the analysis CANON-054 has always required. If `/stats` is only the homepage tile again on its own page, this canon is not met — the tile is the headline, the page is the reporting.

**Metric selection is a per-project design decision, never a studio checklist.** The correct metrics are the ones that are *relevant and valuable to that product's visitors*, and they differ completely across the portfolio. Pick them deliberately; a metric published because it was easy to count, or because every other site publishes it, is the failure mode here. Illustrative, not prescriptive:

| Product shape | Figures that tend to earn their place |
|---|---|
| **Game** | matches or games played · active players · seasons/leagues run · modes played and their split · longest streak · total in-game events (carries, drafts, trades) |
| **App / tool / SaaS** | accounts · things *created* by users (projects, documents, builds, generations) · sessions run · actions completed · uptime · median time-to-result |
| **Website / portfolio / studio** | impressions and unique visitors · projects shipped · releases · commits or sessions run · countries reached |
| **Content / novel** | chapters published · words written · readers reached · reading time delivered |
| **Client services** | engagements delivered · aggregate outcomes · on-time rate |

A **fun** statistic that is genuinely true and genuinely characteristic of the product (total distance travelled in-game, coffee-cups-equivalent of compute, longest session) is explicitly welcome alongside the substantive ones — engagement is a legitimate goal of this surface. It is *not* a licence to relax any honesty rule below; a fun number is held to exactly the same standard as a serious one.

**Liveness contract — "live" means bounded-fresh, not per-visitor-queried.** Live and cost-neutral (CANON-029) coexist in exactly one architecture, and it is the required one: **the site precomputes a stats feed on a schedule; the page reads the feed and refreshes itself from it.** Never query the primary datastore per visitor.

- The project **declares** its own `refreshSeconds` — its honest promise about how fresh the numbers are. There is no studio-wide number: a live multiplayer game may promise 30 seconds; a portfolio site may promise 24 hours. Declaring a slow refresh is fine; *claiming* a fast one you do not meet is a CANON-031 violation.
- The rendered surface **must reflect the promise**: it re-reads the feed at least as often as `refreshSeconds` while the page is open (poll, stream, or revalidate — the mechanism is the project's choice), or, where a page is statically rebuilt on that cadence instead, it says so.
- **Every figure shows its own as-of time**, and a feed older than its declared `refreshSeconds` by a meaningful margin **renders as stale to the reader** — visibly, not silently. A confidently-displayed stale number is worse than an absent one.
- The feed is cached and served as a static artifact. An unbounded live query per visitor is a denial-of-service surface pointed at your own budget and is prohibited.

**Binding to Analytica (CANON-020).** The machine-readable twin this canon has always required **is** the project's **Analytica Feed v1** document (`docs/ANALYTICA_FEED_SPEC.md`, schema `docs/schemas/analytica-feed-v1.json`). One artifact serves three consumers: the homepage tile renders from it, `/stats` renders from it, and Analytica ingests it into the founder dashboard. Projects do not build a second, separate reporting path for the founder — **if the numbers are good enough to show the public, they are the numbers the founder's dashboard reads.** Internal and hybrid projects that publish nothing publicly still emit the same feed shape over a private transport (§ CANON-020), so one schema covers the whole portfolio.

**Report AND analyze — a number alone does not satisfy this canon.** Each published metric carries, at minimum: the value, the period it covers, when it was last computed, and **what it means or how it moved**. A bare counter is telemetry; a counter with a trend, a comparison, or a plain-language reading is analysis. At least one metric per site must carry a genuine interpretation the reader could not have derived from the number alone.

**Honesty rules (CANON-031 applies with full force).** A stats page is the most quotable surface a project has, so it is held to the strictest observability standard in the studio:

- **Never fabricate, extrapolate, or round up.** No placeholder numbers, no "coming soon" values dressed as data, no seeded or demo figures on a live page.
- **Zero is a legitimate published value.** A project with two users publishes two. Suppressing an unflattering number, or waiting to publish until it looks good, is the failure this canon exists to prevent — vanity metrics chosen because they are large are a violation even when each number is individually true.
- **Unmeasured is not zero.** A metric whose source could not be reached renders as unavailable with the reason, never as `0` and never as a stale value presented as current.
- **Every number is dated.** An undated statistic is an undated claim. Staleness past the metric's own declared freshness bar must be visible to the reader, not just to the build.
- **Say what is counted.** "Users" must state whether it means registered accounts, monthly actives, or unique visitors. Ambiguous denominators are how honest numbers become misleading ones.

**Privacy is a hard boundary (CANON-028 and applicable data-protection law).** Published statistics are **aggregate only**. Never publish or make derivable: individual user identities, contact details, internet-protocol (IP) addresses, precise locations, per-user activity, or any figure so small it identifies a specific person. Suppress or band any cell below a small-count threshold. Client-services projects publish client-level numbers **only with that client's explicit permission**; absent permission, aggregate across clients. The founder's personal identity stays out of the numbers.

**Cost discipline (CANON-029).** The stats surface must be cost-neutral at its free tier: precompute to a static artifact on a schedule, serve that artifact, and cache it. A page that runs an unbounded live query per visitor is a denial-of-service surface pointed at your own budget.

**Dual-audience (CANON-048).** The same figures must be machine-readable — a JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) endpoint alongside the human page, referenced from `/agents.json` and `/.well-known/llms.txt`, so agents cite the same numbers humans read rather than scraping them from markup.

**Relationship.** Serves **CANON-031** (observability honesty) as its strictest application; bounded by **CANON-028** (founder identity privacy) and **CANON-029** (free-tier cost discipline); implemented through **CANON-020** (Analytica as the canonical analytics plane) where a project already reports into it; extends **CANON-011** (sitemap standard) with `/stats` as an expected route and **CANON-048** (dual-audience) with a machine-readable twin. A project may satisfy this canon with its own bespoke surface — **CANON-035** (project brand identity) governs how it looks; this canon governs only that it exists and tells the truth.

**Mechanization.** `scripts/check-stats-surface.mjs --project <slug>` verifies the route exists, that published metrics carry value + period + computed-at + interpretation, that a machine-readable twin is declared, and that no metric is undated or unlabelled. **S274 additions:** it also verifies the **homepage showcase tile** is declared with a curated 3–6 metric selection drawn from the feed, that a **liveness contract** (`refreshSeconds` + a declared refresh mechanism) is present and internally consistent, that `/stats` is materially deeper than the tile rather than a copy of it, and that the machine-readable twin conforms to **Analytica Feed v1**. Doctor probe `stats-surface-coverage` reports portfolio adoption; `/app-release-gate` checks it before any SPARKED flip for `public-*` projects.

The checker verifies **structure and honesty affordances, not truthfulness of the underlying counts** — no automated probe can confirm a number is real, so a fabricated statistic is caught by review, not by the gate, and remains a CANON-031 violation. Two S274 limits are worth naming for the same reason: the checker reads the project's *declared* `refreshSeconds`, which proves a promise was made, **not that the deployed page keeps it**; and it compares the tile and page by declared metric composition, which detects a duplicated surface but cannot judge whether the analysis on `/stats` is any good. Both remain review-enforced. Rollback: founder-owned removal of the canon entry, checker, and release-gate hook.

---

## CANON-045 — Obelisk is the unified studio identity + auth plane (one studio account across every project)

**Status:** ACTIVE — S183. | **Last confirmed:** 2026-07-31. | **Effective:** 2026-06-18. | **Source:** Studio Owner directives (S183, S259).

**Decision:** **Obelisk is THE studio-wide security, identity, and authentication plane.** Every VaultSpark surface — every external-facing product site, every internal tool, and the studio website itself — integrates Obelisk so that:
- **One studio account, every project.** A user (human *or* agent) authenticates **once** through Obelisk and carries that identity across the entire portfolio — single sign-on, no per-project account silos. Sign up on any project = a studio account that works everywhere.
- **Human + agent receipts.** Every consequential action (human or agent) produces an Obelisk receipt — a verifiable trust/audit record — extending the package-trust + approval discipline (CANON-023/024) into a portfolio-wide identity ledger.
- **Trust tiers travel with identity.** An account's trust tier (and an agent's AgentDNA trust level) is resolved by Obelisk and honored by every project, rather than re-derived locally.
- **Architecture is explicit.** Every project declares `obeliskArchitecture: internal | external | hybrid`. `internal` gates founder/staff/operator access; `external` gates customer/member accounts; `hybrid` separates both policy realms while retaining one Obelisk identity. This classification controls relying-party registration, policies, consent, session scope, and receipt visibility—it is not inferred from branding or repository visibility.
- **Login and account creation are Obelisk boundaries.** Every applicable sign-in, sign-up, create-account, invitation, recovery, session, and logout flow delegates identity to Obelisk. Projects may own profile/product data, but must not create a competing credential silo or silently fall back to project-local authentication.

**This is a binding target with honest rollout state.** New account-bearing surfaces wire Obelisk before launch; existing projects remain visible as migration gaps until their relying party, flows, trust resolution, and receipts are directly verified. Free studio membership is auto-granted on first studio-account creation unless opted out. The `VAULT_SSO_CONTRACT` is a compatibility surface being folded into / superseded by Obelisk—not permission to build another account plane.

**Obelisk integration is delegate-don't-build (S275, at Obelisk's request).** Projects do **not** build auth per project. The single canonical integration reference is **`obelisk/docs/ECOSYSTEM_ROLLOUT.md`** — three modes (**edge-gate** · **SDK drop-in** · **v1 bridge**), the per-archetype pick, and the deprecations. New integrations use **Passport v2 OIDC** (Authorization Code + S256 PKCE); obtain a `client_id` via `obelisk client create` (or the self-serve `/account/apps` portal), never by hand-editing a registry.

**DEPRECATED — flagged, not deleted, so agents mid-migration understand the change:**
- Hand-rolling WebAuthn/passkeys or an auth engine **inside a project**. Passkeys, MFA, and the login UI belong to the Gate. (This does not deprecate passkeys *at Obelisk itself* — that is the Gate doing its job.)
- Copied Passport **v1** `auth-client.js` / `verify-session` snippets presented as the **primary** integration path. v1 is a measured rollback bridge only.
- Any **per-project account table** carrying `password_hash` / `mfa_secret` / `reset_token`. The correct shape is a single `obelisk_sub` column, JIT-provisioned. A credential column in a product database is the silo this canon exists to prevent.

**Mechanization.** Builds directly on **CANON-021** and **CANON-024**. Canonical integration reference: **`obelisk/docs/ECOSYSTEM_ROLLOUT.md`** (Obelisk owns it; studio-ops points at it rather than forking it, so it cannot drift). Compatibility surface: `docs/VAULT_SSO_CONTRACT.md` → Obelisk identity plane; protocol home `docs/OBELISK_PROTOCOL_PLAN.md` (naming/architecture; **not** the integration how-to). `/initiate` scaffolds Obelisk auth by archetype **by default** — improvised per-project auth is the source of the drift this clause names. Each project records `obeliskArchitecture` + `obeliskAuthStatus`; `/start` Canon reconciliation surfaces missing declarations; `check-release-architecture.mjs` fails unclassified or falsely integrated projects; Console renders the portfolio posture. Rollback is fail-closed access or the last verified Obelisk contract—not a new local credential store.

payload.title: The gate ladder never asked which WRITERS are gated
payload.pattern: Every rung of a gate-audit ladder (has a caller / exists / enforces as claimed) verifies a property OF A GATE. None can detect a WRITER that no gate is pointed at. In statvault, five workflows committed corpus data under [skip ci] — which skips CI by construction, so a bot commit to main is reviewed by nothing — and three ran no contract gate at all.
payload.apply: When auditing whether an invariant is gated, enumerate the PRODUCERS first, then ask which are gated. Assert the gate runs in the same job, BEFORE the write, and can fail it.
pitfalls: Resolve gate delegation FROM SOURCE one level: a workflow whose runner script invokes the gate is correctly gated, and a step-only checker flags it falsely on its first run (the cry-wolf failure that trains bypass).

A gate can be BLIND to a subject rather than lenient about it, and blindness reads as success: my first cut found 4 of 5 writers because its path predicate required a character after data/ and one workflow stages the bare directory. 0 violations printed either way. For any enumerating gate, the COUNT OF SUBJECTS FOUND is itself a claim needing verification.
Declare the required-gate list once; resolve npm aliases through the real package.json rather than a second copy.

payload.title: A test that pins a STATE expires; only a test that pins an INVARIANT is permanent
payload.pattern: Four tests were corrected this session, every one correct when written. The instructive one asserted an accessibility debt ledger was EMPTY — a proxy for the real rule, no violation pre-authorised without a measured run. The ledger own $reopen field named the browser run that would end that emptiness. Left as written, the test made satisfying its own work item STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the task and its test were in direct opposition.
payload.apply: Before deleting or editing a test that newly fails, ask what INVARIANT it stood for and assert that instead. Replacing a proxy with the property it proxied makes the suite stronger; correcting a test weakens it only when the replacement asserts LESS.
pitfalls: A producer test that restates a contract in its own assertions cannot detect a contract the producer never implemented — bind it to the real checker instead, with a negative half proving the pre-fix shape is still rejected.

Naming the wrong CAUSE for a missing measurement is its own dishonesty: a meter reporting 0 entries under the label empty-ledger, when the ledger held 130 entries and a working writer, sent a whole session to build a mechanism that already existed.

# OBELISK IS MANDATORY — implement it in its finalized form (CANON-045, S275)

Obelisk Gate is ONE hosted identity plane, live at https://obeliskgate.com. It runs the entire sign-in ceremony — passkey-first, usernameless, TOTP step-up, magic link, recovery, rate-limiting, lockout, receipts — on its own servers. Every project talks to that one instance.

**DELEGATE, DON'T BUILD.** Do not render your own login form. Do not store password hashes, MFA seeds, or reset tokens. Do not reimplement WebAuthn/passkeys. Do not stand up a per-project account table keyed on email + password. You delegate all of it and receive a cryptographically verified subject (`sub`) you map to your own data.

## Protocol
- Passport v2 — OIDC Authorization Code + **S256 PKCE (mandatory)**. Public clients use auth method `none` and hold NO client secret.
- Discovery: https://obeliskgate.com/.well-known/openid-configuration
- JWKS: https://obeliskgate.com/auth/jwks
- Hosted Universal Login: send the user to `/auth/authorize`; the Gate serves the shared `/auth` experience and redirects back with a code. **You never host a login UI.**
- **Verification happens server-side or edge-side, NEVER in the browser.** The browser can forge anything it alone checks.

## Pick exactly ONE mode per app
| Mode | App auth code | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · Edge-gate | 0 lines | static sites, admin panels, internal tools — reverse-proxy forward-auth against Obelisk OIDC |
| 2 · SDK drop-in | ~3 files | Next.js, Express/Node, Workers, SPAs needing real sessions — `@vaultspark/obelisk-auth` wired to login/callback/logout + verify middleware |
| 3 · v1 bridge | 1 script tag | **DEPRECATED, legacy only** — measured rollback path, never the target |

## Per-archetype recommendation
- next-app / next-src-app → **Mode 2** (`createNextHandlers`; 3 route files + `lib/auth.js`)
- react-spa / vite-spa → **Mode 2** thin BFF (3 backend endpoints; NEVER tokens in localStorage). Pure static admin panel → Mode 1
- static-html → **Mode 1** (0 app code). Need per-user data? add a ~60-line serverless verifier
- workers (Cloudflare) → **Mode 2** worker flavor (SDK core with nodejs_compat, or pure-WebCrypto JWKS verify)
- express / node → **Mode 2** (core + bearer-verify middleware; bring your own session store)
- expo / react-native → **Mode 2** manual OIDC: hand-wire PKCE + HTTPS deep-link callback; tokens in expo-secure-store; backend still verifies every call

## Get a client_id — it is a COMMAND, never a hand-edit
Studio projects submit registration through signed Studio Ark cargo; Obelisk never edits a sibling repo. Operator command:
```
node packages/cli/src/index.js client create --studio \
  --slug=<your-slug> --type=<archetype> \
  --redirect-uri=https://<your-host>/auth/callback
```
It validates RFC 7591 rules, slug/name policy and studio isolation, then prints the exact issuer / authorization / token / client_id / redirect_uri / PKCE / scopes block to paste into your env.

## Environment (Modes 1 & 2)
```
OBELISK_ISSUER=https://obeliskgate.com
OBELISK_CLIENT_ID=          # from `obelisk client create`
OBELISK_REDIRECT_URI=       # the EXACT registered callback (byte-match, https only)
OBELISK_COOKIE_SECRET=      # SDK modes: you generate and hold this; Obelisk never sees it
```

## DEPRECATED — migrate off these
| Wrong way | Why | Migrate to |
|---|---|---|
| Hand-rolled WebAuthn / passkey ceremony | duplicates the Gate's hardened auto-updating ceremony; you own the edge cases AND the breaches | delegate (Mode 1 or 2); delete the local ceremony |
| Copied v1 `auth-client.js` as the primary path | origin-only callback matching; bearer-in-URL risk | register a v2 client_id; move to Mode 1/2; keep `sub` binding |
| Per-project account table with password_hash / mfa_secret / reset_token | the most damaging breach class, and it is Obelisk's job now | drop credential columns; add `obelisk_sub`; JIT-provision by `sub` |
| A second client_id for the worker/API of the same app | shadows the app identity; tenant registry treats it as an isolation violation | ONE app = ONE client_id; verify the same token in the worker |
| Origin-only redirect registration | v2 rejects origin-only matches | register the exact callback URI verbatim |
| Custom-scheme mobile redirect (myapp://) | Gate rejects non-https as unsafe-scheme | HTTPS universal link / App Link |

## Live users (Cohort D) — do not break them
Add Obelisk ALONGSIDE the existing provider, link `obelisk_identity_id` after dual-auth + verified exact email match, make new signups Obelisk-first, flip the default, then retire the old path. **Never force re-enrollment on existing users; never bulk-link by email alone.**

## Why this is cheap to adopt
The plane is centralized: auth screens, OIDC endpoints, token claims, receipts and Rating are SERVED, not copied — Obelisk upgrades reach everyone on a single gate-deploy. The only things pinned on your side are the SDK version and any legacy snippet. Keep those thin.

## What you must do
1. Pick your mode from the archetype table.
2. Request your client_id (Ark cargo to obelisk, or the operator CLI).
3. Wire login/callback/logout; verify server-side.
4. Drop any local credential columns; add `obelisk_sub`.
5. Declare `obeliskArchitecture` (internal|external|hybrid) + `obeliskAuthStatus` in context/PROJECT_STATUS.json — `check-release-architecture.mjs` fails unclassified projects.

Canonical reference: `obelisk/docs/ECOSYSTEM_ROLLOUT.md` (+ integration/QUICKSTART.md, integration/RECIPES.md, CLIENT_REGISTRATION.md). If any other doc or snippet tells you to build auth yourself, that guidance is deprecated.
